subject: Recap + gating questions: deployment topology and custody expectations
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_k@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Gupta <samir.g@clearhealth.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-01T15:03:00-08:00
Subject: Recap + gating questions: deployment topology and custody expectations

Hi Samir — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and the handful of gating questions we promised to put in writing so your procurement and infra teams can review.

Summary of what we heard: ClearHealth needs to run patient PHI inference in a setup that prevents co-mingled customer data, has auditable access logs, and integrates with your Azure KMS. You're evaluating Dedicated reserved capacity vs Private (VPC/on-prem) with an eye to regulatory proof points (SOC2 evidence, pen test reports) and residency in Azure East US.

Gating questions for your team (please reply inline where possible):
- Primary blocking constraint: Is the requirement strict "no shared tenancy" (i.e., must be private control-plane and isolated GPUs) or would Dedicated capacity with tenant isolation + contractual assurances suffice for the first 6–12 months?
- Data residency: must all inference traffic and cached artifacts remain in Azure East US, or are we allowed to use additional AZs/regions for failover?
- KMS / key custody: do you require customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-KMS/HSM) for at-rest encryption, or is Redwoods-managed KMS with key wrapping acceptable temporarily?
- Audit & evidence: please confirm the specific artifacts you need (SOC2 report, penetration test summary, encryption at rest certificate, network diagrams).
- Throughput profile: what is your expected sustained QPS / tokens-per-minute during working hours and expected burst concurrency? This affects placement and Dedicated sizing vs Private sizing.
- Retention & caching: how long can cached KV/prefix artifacts persist? Are there retention limits for logs or telemetry that we should enforce?

Next steps we propose:
1) Provide a short Mutual Action Plan (MAP) listing tech deep-dive, procurement milestones, and SOC2 evidence delivery — we can send by EOD tomorrow.
2) Technical deep-dive with our infra engineer and your security contact (60m) — proposed slots Wed 2026-12-16 10:00 PST or Thu 2026-12-17 14:00 PST.
3) We can produce a Dedicated capacity sizing + ballpark pricing once you give a QPS/token estimate.

Attachments: we can accept your network/data-flow diagram if you want us to confirm isolation implications (feel free to attach).

Thanks — will triage follow-ups as they come.

— Neha
Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
neha_k@redwood.ai

From: Samir Gupta <samir.g@clearhealth.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_k@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kara Jones <kara.jones@clearhealth.ai>, ClearHealth Procurement <procurement@clearhealth.ai>
Date: 2026-12-02T09:21:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Recap + gating questions: deployment topology and custody expectations

Neha — appreciate the recap. Quick answers to the items from our side and an attachment (data_flow_diagram_v2.pdf).

- Tenancy: long term we need no co-mingling of PHI. For an initial pilot (3 months) we could consider Dedicated capacity if there are strong contractual guarantees and technical controls that prevent logical data leakage.
- Residency: must be Azure East US for both inference and short-term KV caches. Failover to a secondary region is acceptable only if it stays within approved geopolitical boundaries and we get prior notice.
- KMS: we require customer-managed keys via our Azure Key Vault HSM integration — this is non-negotiable for any environment touching PHI.
- Evidence: SOC2 Type II report, pen test summary (redacted as needed), and a formal statement of encryption in transit+at-rest.
- Throughput: expected steady-state for pilot is ~250 QPS (average 1.8M tokens / hr) with bursts up to 1k QPS during overnight batch runs.
- Retention: KV/cache should be evicted immediately at session end for PHI workflows; for non-PHI analytics workflows a 24-hour cache is fine. Logs must be retained for 7 years per our policy (we'll provide exact policy text).

We're attaching the data flow diagram. Also looping in Kara (procurement) — Kara, can you share the standard PO language and whether ClearHealth prefers 1yr or 3yr commitments?

Thanks,
Samir
Samir Gupta
Head of ML Engineering, ClearHealth
samir.g@clearhealth.ai

Attachment: data_flow_diagram_v2.pdf

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_k@redwood.ai>, Samir Gupta <samir.g@clearhealth.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-03T11:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Recap + gating questions: deployment topology and custody expectations

Samir / Neha — quick thoughts from sizing/pricing:
- Given the QPS profile (250 steady / 1k bursts), a Dedicated reserved pool sized for the steady-state with burst capacity should work for the pilot. Dedicated gives faster time-to-value and predictable latency.
- Since ClearHealth requires customer-managed KMS and strict residency + long log retention, Private (VPC) is the longer-term, fully compliant target. We typically recommend: pilot on Dedicated (contractually locked down, with encryption + contract clauses), then transition to Private VPC within the first 6–12 months once procurement and network peering are completed.
- For us to build a Dedicated estimate we need: 1) expected peak concurrent tokens, 2) expected request size distribution (avg tokens per request), and 3) any SLA/RTO targets for the pilot.

I can draft a compact pilot SOW + pricing ballpark once we have the above.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Solutions Sales, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

Kara — looping you in on procurement steps and timeline. To make this efficient on our side, can you confirm: 1) preferred PO terms (net 30 / net 45), 2) whether ClearHealth requires a signed MSA + SOW before provisioning Dedicated capacity, and 3) whether ClearHealth has a master reseller or marketplace purchase preference.

Action items we'll take on receipt of confirmation:
- Neha & Ben: draft a 1-page pilot SOW (technical scope, success criteria, timeline) and a Dedicated sizing + ballpark price.
- Legal: put together the MSA + standard security addendum and highlight any redlines we expect.
- Engineering: schedule the technical deep-dive (Neha will propose times).

Proposed slot for the technical deep-dive: Wed 2026-12-16 10:00 PST. Is that still good for you all?

Linking internal MAP / CRM: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/clearhealth

Thanks — will follow up with the SOW draft tomorrow.

— Marissa
